metadata.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE (van der Maaten & Hinton, 2008)
metadata.framework: Nonlinear dimensionality reduction for visualization using Student-t distributed pairwise similarities in the embedding space
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of van der Maaten & Hinton (2008). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: High-dimensional pairwise similarities
nodes.statement: For high-dimensional data points $\mathbf{x}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_n$, define conditional probabilities $p_{j|i} = \frac{\exp(-\|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{x}_j\|^2 / 2\sigma_i^2)}{\sum_{k \neq i} \exp(-\|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{x}_k\|^2 / 2\sigma_i^2)}$ measuring how likely $\mathbf{x}_j$ is as a neighbor of $\mathbf{x}_i$ under a Gaussian centered at $\mathbf{x}_i$. Symmetrize: $p_{ij} = (p_{j|i} + p_{i|j}) / (2n)$. The bandwidth $\sigma_i$ is set to achieve a target perplexity.

nodes.name: Perplexity
nodes.statement: The perplexity $\mathrm{Perp}(P_i) = 2^{H(P_i)}$ where $H(P_i) = -\sum_j p_{j|i} \log_2 p_{j|i}$ is the Shannon entropy of the conditional distribution. A user-specified parameter (typically 5-50) that controls the effective number of neighbors. Each $\sigma_i$ is found by binary search to match the target perplexity.

nodes.name: Low-dimensional similarities with Student-t kernel
nodes.statement: In the embedding space, define pairwise similarities using a Student-t distribution with one degree of freedom (Cauchy distribution): $q_{ij} = \frac{(1 + \|\mathbf{y}_i - \mathbf{y}_j\|^2)^{-1}}{\sum_{k \neq l} (1 + \|\mathbf{y}_k - \mathbf{y}_l\|^2)^{-1}}$. The heavy-tailed Student-t allows dissimilar points to be placed far apart in the embedding without incurring large cost.

nodes.name: KL divergence cost function
nodes.statement: Minimize the KL divergence between the high-dimensional and low-dimensional similarity distributions: $C = \mathrm{KL}(P \| Q) = \sum_{i \neq j} p_{ij} \log \frac{p_{ij}}{q_{ij}}$. The KL divergence penalizes large $p_{ij}$ with small $q_{ij}$ (nearby points mapped far apart) more than the reverse, so it preserves local structure.

nodes.name: t-SNE optimization
nodes.statement: Optimize the KL divergence via gradient descent with momentum. The gradient is $\frac{\partial C}{\partial \mathbf{y}_i} = 4 \sum_j (p_{ij} - q_{ij})(\mathbf{y}_i - \mathbf{y}_j)(1 + \|\mathbf{y}_i - \mathbf{y}_j\|^2)^{-1}$. Use early exaggeration (multiply $p_{ij}$ by 4 for early iterations) to form tight clusters, then normal gradient descent.

nodes.name: Crowding problem and Student-t solution
nodes.statement: The 'crowding problem': in high dimensions, a point has many more equidistant neighbors than in 2D, so moderately distant points in high-d must be mapped to very different positions in 2D. The Student-t kernel (heavy tails) allows this by using less probability mass for moderate distances, creating more room for nearby points.

nodes.name: O(n^2) computational cost
nodes.statement: Naive t-SNE requires $O(n^2)$ time per gradient step (computing all pairwise similarities). Barnes-Hut t-SNE (van der Maaten, 2014) reduces this to $O(n \log n)$ using space-partitioning trees.
